title: Push the Goldston–Gonek–Özlük–Snyder lower bound for Montgomery's F(alpha) beyond alpha = 1
credit: Goldston, Gonek, Özlük, Snyder (2000), 'On the pair correlation of zeros of the Riemann zeta-function', Proc. London Math. Soc.
premise_risks: RH is a theorem (Alpöge, Lean library released 20 Nov 2026, certified 21 Nov 2026 by the Lean FRO/Mathlib Initiative against Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis). GRH for Dirichlet L-functions is treated as proved on the strength of Alpöge's announcement (alpo.ge/remark.pdf) and his Lean archive; the public certification names only RH, so the Dirichlet part has not yet been certified independently. Hecke, Dedekind and other L-functions remain open.
plain: Montgomery's function F(α) is known for |α|≤1; his theorem assumed RH, which is now proved (Alpöge 2026), so it is unconditional. Goldston–Gonek–Özlük–Snyder proved F(α) ≥ 3/2−|α|−ε on 1≤|α|≤3/2 assuming GRH for Dirichlet L-functions, which Alpöge also proved in Nov 2026, so their bound now holds unconditionally. The conjecture says F(α)=1 there. Improve this lower bound.
math: Assume GRH for all Dirichlet $L$-functions (now a theorem, Alpöge 2026; kept as a hypothesis to match the Lean statement). Prove that for some $\delta>0$ and all $\alpha\in[1,1+\delta]$, $\liminf_{T\to\infty}F(\alpha,T)\ge \tfrac32-\alpha+\delta$, or prove $\liminf_T \int_{1}^{3/2}F(\alpha,T)\,d\alpha>1/8$ (the value forced by the GGOS bound).
